runtime_row.subtopic: Trigonometric Ratios of an Acute Angle
runtime_row.questionText: The rod of a TV disc antenna is fixed at right angles to wall AB and a rod CD supports the disc, as shown in the figure. AC = 1.5 m and CD = 3 m. Compute the value of sec θ + cosec θ.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] sec θ = CD/AD = 3/2.6 and cosec θ = CD/AC = 3/1.5 (using AD = 2.6 m from Pythagoras).

fields.questionText: The rod of a TV disc antenna is fixed at right angles to a vertical wall AB, and a rod CD supports the disc. This forms a triangle ACD, right-angled at A, in which AC = 1.5 m, the supporting rod CD = 3 m is the hypotenuse, and θ is the acute angle ∠ADC between CD and AD. Compute the value of sec θ + cosec θ.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] By Pythagoras, AD = √(CD² − AC²) = √(9 − 2.25) = √6.75 = (3√3)/2 m. So sec θ = CD/AD = 3 ÷ (3√3/2) = 2/√3 and cosec θ = CD/AC = 3/1.5 = 2.

first_fixer.rationale: Made self-contained using the row's own diagramDescription (right angle at A, AC=1.5, CD=3 hyp, θ at D). Old 41/13 came from rounding AD to 2.6; exact value is 2+2/√3=(6+2√3)/3≈3.15.
